# SlicerX integrator kit

> SlicerX is a 3D printing slicer (pre-alpha). The main path for a slicer product is to make your own edition (white-label): one edition.config.ts in a clone of the SlicerX repository sets the name, identifiers, theme, fonts and features, and `pnpm edition:build <config> --target desktop` builds a separate app from it with no SlicerX account. Apps can also add pieces in two ways: they start the SlicerX MCP server (@slicerx/mcp) as a child process to slice models, read 3MF projects and list printer, filament and process profiles, and they embed the SlicerX 3D viewport, settings panel and pre-alpha agreement from @slicerx/embed as React components or custom elements, themed with the app's brand. The default path is local: no SlicerX account, no tokens. Cloud slicing and locked projects are optional.

Coding agents: read AGENTS.md first, choose a path (A: your own edition, B: embed and drive pieces, C: an installed SlicerX), then follow its steps in order (packages, MCP connection, interview, build, agreement, theming, checks). Build the local path first; read the optional cloud and locked-projects section only if the user asks. An AI client never approves a print start, a resume, raw G-code or a printer adjustment. Tokens never go in code.

## Docs

- [restyle-icons-and-loops.md](restyle-icons-and-loops.md): recolor edition icons, tooltip loops and sketch glyphs with shared, light and dark config values; token defaults and build checks

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): step-by-step instructions for coding agents, with MCP setup per client, the interview, recipes, theming and the rules
- [Credit kit](credit-kit/README.md): "Made possible by SlicerX" badges, a Support SlicerX button, copy to paste, usage rules and screenshots
- [../integrating.md](../integrating.md): the long guide to building your own edition, with a worked example
- [partner-app-key.md](partner-app-key.md): reaching the user's printers through SlicerX's bridge with a partner app key the user makes and revokes
- [connected-apps.md](connected-apps.md): Spoolman, Home Assistant and BamBuddy through SlicerX's bridge: MCP tools, approvals, the Home Assistant domains, adding a new app, and a runnable sample in connected-apps/
- [engine-path.md](engine-path.md): Path B with the sx engine instead of the MCP server for slicing: Prepare tools in the viewport, the plate as a slice request, settings (a request without the printer's settings slices on engine defaults with a `no_machine_profile` warning), exit codes and the preview
- [whats-new-0.1.5.md](whats-new-0.1.5.md): what engine 0.1.5 changed for integrators, and what is not in it yet
- [mimir-cloud.md](mimir-cloud.md): mimir cloud for an app with its own mimir chat: register with the edition's key, the Messages API allowlist (pinned model, thinking and server tool blocks passed back, base64 images, size limits), quota in millionths of a dollar, forget, sharing headers, refusals (never auto-retry a 429) and a fake server for tests
- [your-own-mimir.md](your-own-mimir.md): an edition's own mimir under `ai.brain`: the voice, its own knowledge, tool groups, routing for a person's own key, cloud step-up, memory and sync, and the `slicerx_mimir_brain` read-back
- [your-own-mimir.md#print-runs](your-own-mimir.md#print-runs): print runs in an edition's mimir: what switching off the printers or design group removes, reading a run with `slicerx_mimir_run`, why an integrator never starts a print, and the busy printer rule
- [holes.md](holes.md): `slicerx_geom_hole`, making a round hole another size (diameter, depth, counterbore or countersink) on a design or an STL, picked by its axis or its wall, with the hole read back before and after
- [edge-drag.md](edge-drag.md): drag a part past a bed edge to send it to another plate with `@slicerx/viewport/edge-drag`: the plate adapter (plates, active plate, move with undo, drop target, obstacles), theming with `--sx-edge-*` properties, labels, accessibility and a check list
- [quickstart.md](quickstart.md): the reference for the server options, tools, settings layers, result fields, progress, token scopes and error codes
- [updates.md](updates.md): staying current: build from desktop-v or engine-v release tags, read each release's "For editions and integrations" section, and watch the urgent and integrators labels between releases

## Packages

- [Assistant branding](assistant-brand.md): edition name, icon and light/dark accent, setAssistantName for embedded packages, and MCP/CLI read-back

- @slicerx/mcp: the MCP server; `node_modules/@slicerx/mcp/dist/cli.js`, or `require.resolve('@slicerx/mcp/cli')`. `slicerx_slice_file` and `slicerx_estimate_file` take the printer, process and filament in `profiles` (`"profiles": ["machine:snapmaker-u1", "process:standard"]`); `printer` or `process` arguments are ignored with an `ignored_arguments` warning. `placement: "keep"` slices a 3MF's parts where the file puts them instead of centering the plate, and refuses a part off the bed (`invalid_input`, `details.reason` `off_bed`); in an `sx slice --request` request it is `plate.placement`, exit 3 when refused. Local AI tools: `slicerx_local_ai_check` (read), `slicerx_local_ai_setup` (always asks the user; downloads through Ollama), `slicerx_local_ai_status` (read)
- @slicerx/embed: Viewport, SettingsPanel, Agreement, LocalAiSetup and useLocalAi (Set up local AI), EmbedTheme, createTheme, the custom elements, and `@slicerx/embed/sxlock` for optional locked projects
- @slicerx/viewport: the three.js viewport under Viewport

## Optional

- [Embedding the engine](../embedding.md): the Rust crate, the sx CLI, the C ABI and WebAssembly
